chapter_title: The Chapter of the Elements that wept
spiritual_reading:
#
 Spiritual
 Translation
 of the Four
 Griefs of
 the External
 Truths

---


**
¶2.
** The external truths that
 proceed from the Lord
's Divine Love — the
 first
 and
 in
most good
 from
 which all protecting
 truths desc
end — suffered
 deep
 spiritual
 
anguish three times.
 Then they were
 st
illed
. There remains a fourth 
anguish, for they shall grieve
 at the final
 consummation of all things. And
 after
 that
, their suffering
 shall cease, and never
 again shall they know
 grief from that time on
ward.

---


**¶3.** The
 first anguish came
 when they perceived the whole
 realm
 of falsity —
 the power of evil preparing
 to e
rupt against them. They comprehended everything
 that would befall them in the
 combat
 of spiritual life
. They perceived the evil that would rise
 and come
 upon them, yet by divine necessity they
 advanced toward it and engaged it. They
 prevailed over it, they held it
 fast. They bound it by
 means
 of their own exterior forms and their
 out
ward expressions of
 truth
.
 They overcame its spiritual death,
 its self-love, and its fals
ity.

Here
 the
 external
 truths proce
eding from the Lord
's in
most love
 enter
 volunt
arily into conjunction
 with evil
, not
 from
 ignor
ance but
 from fore
knowledge. They know
 the nature
 of what
 they face
, yet
 necessity
 —
 the necessity
 of divine
 order
,
 which
 requires
 that good
 and truth con
front
 and
 subj
ugate evil — drives them forward
. They overcome
 the
 thre
efold enemy
:
 spiritual
 death, which
 is the extinction
 of all
 heav
enly life
; self-love, which is the
 fire
 that cons
umes from
 within; and falsity, which is
 the darkness that blind
s the understanding
.
 They bind
 these
 by
 wr
apping them within
 their own forms —
 for
 this
 is how
 external
 truths operate:
 they contain
 and
 rest
rain evil
 by
 encomp
assing it.

---

**
¶4.** The second angu
ish came when the Lord
 as
 Divine
 Love —
 the in
most good from which they
 proceeded — ascended out of the deep
est states
 of falsity and departed from them;
 that is, when He div
ested
 Himself of them and left them in the
 lower states of
 the
 mind
. When they perceived that the Divine Love
 had risen from the a
byss of
 fals
ity and had
 gone
 on
 without
 them —
 that
 they
 were
 left behind amid
 the hostility of
 evil
 — they grieved and were angu
ished in their in
most
 being
. Yet what could they do?
 They surrendered their inter
iors to every affl
iction. They remained behind
 and grew spiritually feeble under
 the pressure
 of the
 imm
ense burden
 of all the works of reformation, until
 the time
 of cons
ummation.

This
 corresponds
 to the state
 in
 which the Lord
's
 inmost love
,
 having
 descended
 into the deepest confront
ation with the
 h
ells
, withdraw
s up
ward —
 but
 the
 external
 truths that served
 as His
 instruments
 in
 that
 descent
 are
 not yet
 capable
 of following
. They are left
 within
 the natural
 degree
 of the mind, still
 surrounded
 by the resistance
 of evil, bearing
 the full
 weight of the regener
ative
 work
 that
 must be accomplished
 over
 time
. Their
 grief is that of
 tru
ths separated
 from their
 origin
 —
 truths that know
 the good
 from
 which they came
, yet find
 themselves lab
oring in states
 far
 removed
 from it
.

---

**¶5
.** The third anguish came
 when the Lord as
 Divine Spiritual Truth set
 aside the three external
 truths of active operation, placing them
 beneath all the
 states of the
 mind. He gave them a
 sign —
 an
 infl
ux of perception
 — to lift their understanding and rise
 toward
 the interior and
 elevated
 states from that condition; and
 to pass through all the
 natural states of the mind until they should
 reach the state of heavenly tran
quility and peace, the place of
 spiritual
 rest prepared for them. When they perceived
 that He had separated
 Himself from them,
 and
 that they themselves
 remained behind and
 had not yet ascended — at that
 moment these three external truths grieved
. After their grief, they turned their
 interiors toward all the elevated states of
 wisdom
 that had been conce
aled from them, and came into unity
 of will. For they would so
ar up
ward and come
 into
 the interior
 states, passing through all things until the
 time that
 was ordained for them at the consumm
ation of
 all
 states
.

Here
 the separation
 is
 enacted
 a
 second time,
 but
 now
 by
 the Divine
 Spiritual Truth rather
 than the Divine
 Love. The three
 external truths of active operation —
 those
 tru
ths through
 which the work
 of regeneration is carried out in
 the natural
 mind — are deliberately
 set beneath
 all
 other
 states as
 a
 foundation
. They
 are given the
 promise
 of
 eventual
 ascent:
 a
 sign,
 meaning
 an
 interior
 perception
 that
 their
 condition
 is not
 final
.
 Their
 grief yields
 to resolution
.
 They turn in
ward, they un
ify their will
, and they set
 themselves
 toward
 the heights
.
 This
 is
 the state
 of tru
ths that have
 accepted
 their
 role
 as the
 lowest
 servants
 of the divine
 order,
 knowing
 that their
 labor
,
 though
 prolong
ed, has
 a
 cons
ummation prepared
 for them in
 heav
enly peace.

---

**
¶6.** The fourth angu
ish comes
 when the Grand Human — the completed
 divine
 form composed
 of all who have
 received
 good
 and truth — is
 taken up at the final
 consummation.
 Then
 the external truths shall
 grieve,
 not
 for themselves
, but for those souls
 who are
 in deliber
ate falsification and profanation of
 truth
. For
 their spiritual members have been severed —
 the
 living
 connections
 by
 which they might
 have been
 joined
 to the whole — and they
 have
 passed
 into fals
ity entirely
. And those souls themselves
, when the Grand Human ascends and
 they are left utt
erly alone, shall grieve because they
 remain behind in affl
iction forever. For they are
 cut off and separated from the completed Divine
 Human Form. And it is a
 necessity of
 divine
 order to
 cons
ign those
 souls who have
 prepared
 themselves
 for spiritual
 perd
ition to the
 retribution that
 corresponds
 to the
 deeds they have done. They enter
 into falsity and are bound with fals
ity —
 precisely
 as they desired it
 and loved it, and as
 they placed the
 treasure of their will within it. At
 the very
 moment when the Grand
 Human rises
, they shall cry
 out,
 because
 they are severed from the communion of
 this great completed
 form
. And they remain behind forever. This
 great anguish is terrible.
 It stands
 before
 those
 souls who are prepared
 for perdition according to their works.
 And they shall grieve with that grief
 and
 never fall
 silent,
 because
 rest
 shall not
 come to them from
 that
 time onward.

This
 is
 the state of final
 separation:
 the cons
ummation in
 which the whole
 of the heav
enly human
 form —
 every
 soul con
joined to good
 and truth — is gathered up
 and completed
. Those
 who
 have loved
 fals
ity and profaned
 truth are not
 destroyed
 by
 external
 punishment
 but
 by the withdrawal
 of all
 that
 could
 have sustained
 spiritual
 life. They are bound
 with what
 they chose
.
 Their
 tor
ment is the
 perpet
ual rest
lessness of a
 will
 that has placed
 its
 love
 in
 what
 cannot
 satisfy
,
 cannot
 give
 peace
, cannot cease
 its
 burning
. They cry
 out because they perce
ive,
 at
 the last
,
 what
 they have lost
 —
 communion
 with the living
 whole
 of
 heaven
 — and this
 perception
,
 unlike
 all
 prior
 grief
, is without
 end
,
 because no
 further
 state
 of
 reformation
 remains
.


---

**¶7.
** Thus
 these external
 truths belong
 to the fundamental spiritual substances
 from
 which all things of
 the mind are composed. This fourth grief
 is heart-rending for them beyond
 all the
 others. It is far more
 grievous than the three preceding 
anguishes. For
 in
 this fourth time, their
 grief is not for themselves —
 they
 have
 passed
 through
 their
 own
 trials
 and are restored
.
 Rather, they grieve and are 
anguished on
 behalf of those souls who will be cut
 off from peace forever
, because no
 rest shall ever
 come to rel
ieve them from their torment.


This
 final
 passage
 reveals
 the deep
est correspondence
:
 the external truths themselves
,
 having
 served
 as the instruments of the Lord's descent
,
 combat
,
 and reformation
 —
 having
 suffered
 separation
,
 labor
, and patient
 endurance through
 three
 great
 cycles
 of grief
 — arrive
 at last
 at a
 grief
 that is purely
 compass
ionate. Their own
 restoration
 is complete
. What
 remains is the s
orrow of
 heaven
 itself over
 those
 who cannot
 be saved
:
 the grief
 of truths that were
 offered
 to
 all
,
 accepted
 by some
, and rejected utt
erly by others. This is the we
eping of heaven
 at
 the final judgment
 —
 not
 the
 weeping of loss
, but the weeping of love
 that can
 do
 no more.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: The garments, the sons of the First Man, wept bitterly three times. Then they were silent. There is a fourth time of weeping, for they will weep at the end. And then their crying can stop, and they will never again weep from this time on.

Now, the first time of their weeping is when they had seen the darkness, the enemy being about to burst out against them. They understood everything that would happen to them. They were aware of the one that would rise and come upon them, but by necessity they hastened to him and fought with him. They mastered him, they detained him. They bound him with their body and their limbs, they overcame his death and his fire and his darkness.

[The] second time that they wept is [when the]ir father, the First Man, [ascend]ed from the [abyss] of darkness and left them behind; that is the time when he stripped [them off] and left them below. Indeed, when th[ey] s[aw] how the First Man had risen out of the abyss and [l]eft them behind, and that they were abandoned in the enmit[y, th]ey wept and were sore of heart. Still, what could they do, wishing [to give] their heart to every affliction. They [remained b]ehind and grew [s]ick under the pressure of the weighty burden of all the works, until the end time.

[The] third time that they wept is when the Living Spirit stripped off the three garments of activity, placing them beneath all things. He gave them a sign to lift their heads and rise to the heights from that place; and to pass and journey through all the earths until they should reach the land of tranquilli[t]y and peace, the place of rest prepared for them. So, when they had seen him, that he had separated himself from them, while they themselves remained behind after him and had not ascended; at that moment when they stayed behind these three garments wept. After their crying, they turned their [hear]t to all the heights that were concealed from them, and were of one mind. For [they would] soar up and come to the heights; and pass over all things until the time that was ordained for them all [should be fulfilled] at the end of the worlds.

So, they too are the garments of these elements. This fourth time of weeping is heart-rending for them. It is much worse for them than these other three times of weeping before. This fourth time the weeping is not for themselves. Rather they weep and are heartsore for these soul[s] who will be cut off from peace, because rest will not come about for them, to allow them to rest from torment for ever.

[The f]ourth time when they will weep is when the [S]tatue will be taken up on the last day, and they will weep [for] the souls of the liars and blasphemers; for they may give [ ... ] because their limbs have been severed [ ... ] of the darkness. And also [th]ose souls, when the Statue will go up and th]ey are left alo[n]e, they will weep in that they will rema[in] behind in affliction for ever. For they wi[ll be cut off] and separated from the Last Statue. An[d it is] a necessity to take these souls who are ready for loss as retribution for the deeds that they have done. They go i[n to] this [darkne]ss and are bound with the darkness; just as they desired it and loved it, and placed their treasure with it. At that very moment, when the Last Statue rises up, the[y wi]ll weep. And then they will scream out loud because they will be severed from the company of this great Statue. And they remain behind for ever. This great weeping [ ... ] is terrible, it occurs in front of the souls and [ ... ] who are ready for loss in accordance with their deeds. And they [will] weep with that crying, they will never be silent; because they will not attain rest from this time on.
